key_insight: A PINN solves the specific Couette-flow case most accurately, but a data-driven DeepONet is far better for fast, reusable prediction across changing slip and wall-speed conditions.
engineering_relevance: The study shows that surrogate ML models can enable near-real-time fluid-flow forecasting and rapid parametric exploration where repeated high-fidelity simulation would be too slow.
method: PINN: physics-informed solver for the governing equations with dynamic wall slip.
DeepONet: trained on Crank-Nicolson-generated data to learn the solution operator over varying boundary conditions.
Benchmarking against a numerical solver to compare accuracy, generalization, and inference speed.
evidence_signal: Reported performance includes 0.083% relative L2 error for the PINN, 0.36% mean relative error on unseen DeepONet cases, 0.88% on out-of-distribution signals, and about a 540X speedup over the numerical solver.
watch_item: The PINN is highly case-specific and requires retraining for new conditions, while the DeepONet depends on the coverage and quality of its training data for reliable extrapolation.
paper_title: Solution of the Newtonian plane Couette flow with dynamic wall slip using machine-learning methods
